title: NVDA Stock Gains After-Hours: Board Chairman Harvey Jones Confirms Huang Will Not Be Reinstated As Nvidia Puts Forth Expectation-Beating Outlook

NVDA Stock Gains After-Hours: Board Chairman Harvey Jones Confirms Huang Will Not Be Reinstated As Nvidia Puts Forth Expectation-Beating Outlook

Nvidia reported record Q3 revenue of $115.8 billion, up 103% year over year, driven by strong data center sales and the rapid rollout of its Vera Rubin platform.

The chipmaker forecast fourth-quarter fiscal 2027 revenue of $130 billion, beating Wall Street estimates.

Interim CEO Colette Kress raised the chipmaker's 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%, up from 70% during the earnings call.

Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) share price gained about 2% after-hours on Tuesday after the chipmaker delivered a stronger-than-expected sales forecast and record quarterly revenue, signaling resilient demand for the firm's silicon as the company wades through a leadership transition.

In its first financial update since severing ties with Jensen Huang last week, the Santa Clara-based chipmaker reported revenue of $115.8 billion for its fiscal third quarter ended Oct. 25, a 103% jump from a year earlier, topping analyst projections of $109.3 billion.

Earnings came in at $2.68 per share, beating analyst estimates of $2.47.

On the earnings call, Nvidia's chairman of the board, Harvey Jones, declined to make any comment regarding Jensen Huang's exit and emphasized on the fact that the board will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia.

Nvidia's Data Center Boom

Nvidia's data center division continued to contribute the most to overall revenues, generating $107.6 billion in third-quarter revenue, up 110% from a year ago and surpassing analyst estimates of $101.9 billion.

While the revenue blew past expectations, it recorded a mild drop in growth compared to the previous quarter, when data center revenues grew 116.6%. The drop was also the first quarterly drop in data center revenue growth since the quarter ending July 2025.

Nevertheless, the unit brought in more revenue during the quarter than rivals Intel Corp. (INTC) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD) generate in an entire year combined.

Nvidia Q3 data center revenue growth

The surge was propelled by the production ramp and initial shipments of the Nvidia Vera Rubin, which Kress described as the fastest product ramp in company history.

"Vera Rubin is the fastest product ramp in Nvidia's history, already tallying up $20 billion in revenue," Kress told during the earnings call.

Major cloud providers, including CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, and Nebius, have already deployed Vera Rubin systems.
